function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

Below you’ll find two common ways to pull **all node‑level data** from a Fabric called *“test‑de”* when your controller/API gateway sits at **IP 23.31.32.1**. Pick whichever fits your environment – either a simple *RESTCONF* query (the most “API‑first” approach) or a quick *CLI* snapshot if you’re already logged into a switch/router that hosts the fabric database. --- ## 1️⃣ RESTCONF / JSON API (Cisco DNA Center style) | Step | What to do | Example | |------|------------|---------| | **A. Build the request URL** | Most controllers expose topology under `/api/node/class/.json`. For all fabric nodes:
`https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/fabricNode.json` | N/A | | **B. Add filter for the fabric name** | Append a JMESPath filter (`?$query=`). To restrict to `"test-de"`:
``$query={"name":"eq.test-de"}`` | `https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/fabricNode.json?$query=%7B%22name%22:%20%22eq.test-de%22%7D` | | **C. Authenticate & send** | Basic Auth (or token), HTTPS, ignore cert errors during dev.
curl -sk -u : ""
| ```bash
curl -sk -u admin:admin123 \\\n "https://23.31.32.1/api/node/class/fabricNode.json?\$query={\"name\":\"eq.test-de\"}"\``` | ### Sample Response Snippet ```json { "imdata": [ { "fabricNode": { "@dn": "uni/fabric/domains/domain-[test-de]/nodes/node-101", "@id": "101", "@name": "test-de-node01", "@role": "leaf", "@state": "active", ... } }, { "fabricNode": { ... } # next node … } ] } ``` #### Fields worth noting | Field | Meaning | |-------|--------| | `@id` | Node numeric ID | | `@name` | Human‑readable hostname | | `@role` | leaf/spine/etc. | | `@state` | operational state (e.g., active, down) | | `@dpktCount`, `@rxBytes`, … | Optional counters (if requested via `$expand`) | If you only care about status, add `&$select=@id,@name,@role,@state` to keep payload small. --- ## 2️⃣ CLI Snapshot (NX‑OS / IOS XE) If you have console access to a device that holds the fabric DB (often a spine router): ```text ssh admin@23.31.32.1 enable terminal length 0 ! Show everything without paging show fabric nodes detail ! Common NX‑OS command ``` Typical output looks like: ``` Fabric Name : test-de ------------------------------------ ID Role Hostname State ------------------------------------------------- 101 Leaf test-de-leaf01 Active 102 Spine test-de-spine01 Active 103 Leaf test-de-leaf02 Down ... ``` For **IOS XE**, replace the command with something similar such as: ```text show cisco-nxos-fabric nodes ``` (Exact wording depends on vendor.) --- ## Quick Script (Python + Requests) ```python import json, sys, urllib.parse from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth import requests BASE_URL = "https://23.31.32.1" FABRIC_NAME = "test-de" url = f"{BASE_URL}/api/node/class/fabricNode.json" params = {"$query": json.dumps({"name": f"eq.{FABRIC_NAME}"})} resp = requests.get(url, params=params, auth=HTTPBasicAuth("admin", "admin123"), verify=False) # skip SSL check for demo print(json.dumps(resp.json(), indent=2)) ``` Run it after installing `requests`: ```sh pip install requests python get_nodes.py ``` --- ## Troubleshooting Checklist | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | No rows returned | Wrong fabric name spelling | Double‑check case/special chars | | Authentication error | Wrong credentials or missing role | Verify username/password and ACL | | Timeout / connection refused | Controller unreachable | Ping 23.31.32.1, ensure port 443 open | | Unexpected schema | Using older firmware version | Update docs or adjust class names (`topoNode` vs `fabricNode`) | --- That’s basically it—pick the method that matches your tooling stack and you’ll see all nodes belonging to **fabric test‑de** right away!
